question: At 5% per annum rate of compound interest the amount Rs. 4,000 after 24 months will become ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of Compound Interest for 2 years at 5% p.a. = 5 + 5 + (5 × 5) ÷ 100 = 10.25%

Amount after 2 years = Principal × (100% + 10.25%)

⇒ Amount = 4000 × 110.25%

⇒ Amount = 4000 × (110.25 ÷ 100)

⇒ Amount = 4410

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 4,410.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 4,000

Rate (R) = 5% per annum

Time (T) = 24 months = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)T

 Compound Interest Progression

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount = 4000 × (1 + 5 ÷ 100)²

⇒ Amount = 4000 × (105 ÷ 100)²

⇒ Amount = 4000 × (21 ÷ 20) × (21 ÷ 20)

⇒ Amount = 4000 × (441 ÷ 400)

⇒ Amount = 10 × 441 = 4410

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 4,410.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate for 2 Years

If the rate of interest is R% per annum, the effective compound interest rate for 2 years can be directly calculated as Rₑff = 2R + (R² ÷ 100)%.

Difference Between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a principal P is calculated as Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate of interest is halved (R ÷ 2) and the time period is doubled (2T).
